newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM denies selling Nokia stake.
newsitem.headline: UPM denies selling Nokia stake.

text.p: Europe's largest forestry group UPM-Kymmene on Tuesday denied market speculation late in the share trading session that it was divesting its stake in compatriot Finnish telecoms group Nokia.
"Rumours are rumours," Jan-Hendrik Kulp, the group's Chief Financial Officer, told Reuters by telephone. "Our only comment is that there is no decision to sell."
He was speaking after brokers in the Nordic area and abroad cited speculation that UPM, Nokia's second-largest shareholder at end-1996, had sold or was selling its stake in the telecoms group.
A Nokia spokesman said he had heard nothing about such a plan and noted that such a transaction would be very large.

Some brokers said they were inferring UPM may be a seller after being offered larger than usual quantities of Nokia stock. But one analyst, requesting anonymity, said the talk was just "a damn good rumour."
The talk surfaced just as Helsinki was closing and appeared to have no impact on Nokia's stock here, which shadowed a late uptick to end up 3.00 markka at 380.00 markka.
Nokia's ADR in New York was probing year-high ground, up $2 1/8 at $74, after touching 74 1/8.
UPM-Kymmene also followed Helsinki stocks up just before the close, ending at 122.00 markka, up 1.50.
In Nokia's 1996 annual report the telecoms company listed UPM-Kymmene as its second-largest shareholder with 11.6 million K and A series shares or 3.9 percent of the stock, and 9.7 percent of votes.

Analysts said market speculation had been partly fuelled by comments made by UPM-Kymmene management to analysts after its 1996 report, that the stake in Nokia was not core for UPM. Talk it may sell its stake resurfaced from time to time.
UPM has recently started reducing its holding in engineering group Rauma.
UPM CEO Juha Niemela said in March the company's main short-term goal was to reduce its indebtedness.
